code_inspection.scope: Notebook read through all cells: In[1]-In[7], final unexecuted ERC backtest cell and final blank cell. Toolkit inspected specifically risk_contribution, target_risk_contributions, equal_risk_contributions and weight_erc. No source cells run or source files redistributed.
findings: Risk contribution helper returns w*(Sigma*w)/(w*Sigma*w), a fractional allocation. Raw volatility Euler contributions use a different denominator.

The course fits squared differences from target risk shares by SLSQP; this fractional objective is nonlinear, not a quadratic program. Our positive-budget examples use a convex log-barrier construction and check residuals.
Lab compares rolling 36-month EW/CW and introduces ERC; its final ERC backtest cell is unexecuted in the inspected notebook. Our rolling comparison is original and simulated.

conventions: ENC describes long-only capital concentration; asset labels need not represent independent risk sources.
Volatility Euler components sum to volatility; variance allocations sum to variance; the weight times raw variance derivative instead sums to twice variance.
Negative risk contributions are signed hedging effects; risk shares are undefined at zero portfolio variance.
Inverse volatility equals ERC only under stated covariance conditions; arbitrary correlations require solving the budget problem.
Minimum ENC is a capital-concentration constraint; maximum decorrelation and maximum diversification ratio use distinct objectives.
Risk budgets and forecast volatility rely on estimated covariance; equality in the model does not ensure equal realized risk.
Backtest weights use only preceding observations; gross/net comparisons share weights, horizons and starting capital.
